title: Rapamycin for Longevity: Complete Clinical Guide (2026) | Hillary Lin, MD | Hillary Lin, MD | Hillary Lin, MD
abstract: The interpretation was that low-dose, intermittent mTOR inhibition partially reverses age-related immune decline — the opposite of what transplant-dose rapamycin does. The appropriate interpretation: PEARL showed that low-dose rapamycin is likely safe over a year in healthy adults, with some secondary signals of benefit — particularly for women. **Biweekly dosing (every 14 days)** Some physicians use every-two-week dosing — lower cumulative mTOR suppression, more conservative immune profile, useful for patients with infection concerns or metabolic sensitivity. ### How is rapamycin dosed for longevity, and why weekly instead of daily? ### Does rapamycin suppress the immune system at longevity doses? A 2014 study found that low-dose intermittent rapamycin analog improved flu vaccine responses in older adults by 20% relative to placebo — suggesting partial reversal of age-related immune decline rather than suppression. The mouse lifespan data suggests late-life starting is still effective — the ITP found significant lifespan extension when rapamycin was started at 20 months (approximately equivalent to age 60 in humans).
